publication_status.evidence: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1051/0004-6361/201629260 returns A&A volume 601, issued 2017-04-25 for this title; bibcode from the VizieR ReadMe J/A+A/601/A34 (checked 2026-10-14). Element values are read from the Fig. A.7 panel of the arXiv:1608.03525 PDF ('A&A proofs'), not from a table: the brief's 'Table 4' is not what the arXiv version calls it. The published version might differ in the last digit.

method: Two unresolved stars fitted to each night of AMBER (amdlib 3), PIONIER (pndrs) or GRAVITY (ESO pipeline) data: free parameters are the two sky coordinates and the H-band flux ratio, the latter held constant over H and over epochs; orbital motion is neglected within a night (Sect. 2.3). Orbit: Levenberg-Marquardt on the resolved positions and the SB2 radial velocities together, ten parameters (P, T, a, e, i, Omega, omega of the secondary, Ka, Kb, gamma), with a constant 10.0 km/s RV shift between the components that the fit needed (Sect. 3.7). No priors.
flux_ratio_definition: f_H = secondary / primary, H band, the secondary being the star faint in H (Sect. 2.3). f_H = 0.62 +/- 0.02 (Fig. A.7 panel; Fabry+21 Sect. 2.2 quotes the same). One value for all epochs. Not measured in K; the NACO Ks flux in design/plan_eso_binaries.md sat at its bound of 1, against this 0.62.
uncertainties: Orbital uncertainties are the rms of fits to datasets corrupted by random additive noise of the quoted size (Sect. 2.5). Add a 1.5% systematic on a from the PIONIER effective-wavelength calibration. Per-epoch positions have error ellipses only. Le Bouquin+17 (Table B.1 caption, CDS ReadMe note 3) calls emax/emin the FWHM of the error ellipse's axes; Fabry+21 (Table A.2 caption) calls the same numbers 1-sigma. They cannot both be right: the factor is 2 sqrt(2 ln 2) = 2.3548. Stored as published; do not convert before the first blind fit shows which reading gives pulls of order 1.

conventions.PA: north through east; position of the secondary (faint in H) relative to the primary (bright in H), separation in mas (Table B.1 caption)
conventions.omega: argument of periastron of the secondary, from the ascending node along the motion of the secondary; the ascending node is the node where the motion is directed away from the observer (Sect. 2.4). Same star and sense as virgil's omega (the companion's, node where it recedes), so omega_shift_deg = 0. Checked independently: crosscheck.orbits evaluated at the 18 published epochs with these elements (a = 14.78 mas, T + 3P) reproduces them to 0.19 mas rms (0.49 mas worst, against error-ellipse major axes of 0.12-2.1 mas), with the position angle increasing in time for i < 90 deg.
conventions.Omega: longitude of the ascending node, in the plane of the sky, from north through east (Sect. 2.4). With no radial velocities Omega and omega are only fixed modulo 180 deg together; here the RVs fix them.
conventions.inclination: i > 90 deg would mean a clockwise apparent orbit. 9 Sgr has i = 86.64 deg: counter-clockwise, PA increasing.
conventions.T: T = 46613 +/- 21 MJD, a periastron passage of the secondary long before the data; T + 3P = 56544.2 falls inside them, against Fabry+21's T0 = 56547 +/- 12. Both are MJD. Only T modulo P matters.

error_ellipse_published.convention: FWHM per Le Bouquin+17, 1-sigma per Fabry+21: see conventions.uncertainties

orbit.headline: Le Bouquin+17, combined astrometry + SB2 radial velocities (Fig. A.7 panel)
T_peri_mjd: published T; T + 3P = 56544.2 is the periastron inside the data

from_apparent_orbit_and_RVs.note: the mass tension: far below the O3.5V + O5.5V masses (~50 + 34), which Fabry+21 resolved

orbit.source: Fig. A.7 panel (p. 16 of the arXiv:1608.03525 PDF)

other_published_orbit.label: Fabry+21 (arXiv:2105.09968), astrometry of 23 epochs: LB17's 18, three GRAVITY, two new PIONIER
omega_deg: the relative orbit's, i.e. the secondary's: Table 1 note (a) says it is shifted by 180 deg from the primary's omega_1 used for RV curves
a_mas: DERIVED, not published: Fabry+21 does not tabulate a_app. From Eq. 6 inverted, a_app = (G M P^2 / 4 pi^2)^(1/3) / d with M = 92 Msun (K1 = 36, K2 = 49 km/s), P = 3261 d, d = 1310 pc. Circular, since their d came from the same a_app. Another reading of Table A.2 (design/plan_eso_binaries.md) gave 14.656 mas.
other_published_orbit.MCMC: 100000 samples with spinOS; uncertainties are 1-sigma intervals (Table 1 caption)

other_papers.bibcode: 2021A&A...651A.119F (from the task statement; A119 not in Crossref's article-number field)
other_papers.role: refit: resolves the dynamical-mass tension. Adds three GRAVITY (PMOIRED fits, 0.1 mas systematic added in quadrature) and two PIONIER epochs (2017-05, 2017-08).
the SB2 radial-velocity orbit and the periastron-passage X-ray study: source of the old mass/inclination tension

eso_data.checked: 2026-10-14, ESO TAP dbo.raw and ivoa.ObsCore, by object name and a 36 arcsec box
eso_data.phase3: PIONIER ADP products exist for 2016-08-01 (MJD 57601.209 and 57601.219), 2017-05-27 and 2017-08-30 only (pndrs-reduced OIFITS)
beyond_the_papers: GRAVITY 099.D-0777(B), 2017-06-22 (MJD 57926.297), one object frame and no sky or calibrator: a possible post-publication epoch
AMBER 085.C-0389(B), 2010-06-09, 75 frames: in neither paper's table

notes: Data come from the ESO archive as raw frames; virgil never sees the published positions. The OiDB PIONIER L2 collection is private and unused.
